subject: AMD ROCm.AI, AMD Skills, and ROCm CLI v0.1.0-experimental.1

selection.reason: AMD moved part of its GPU software onboarding and model-serving workflow into agent-readable skills and a downloadable CLI. The announcement, immutable code, exact release tag, installer, checksums, and skill scripts support a scoped engineering conclusion while exposing material Tech Preview limits.

signals.note: Reviewed recent OpenAI, Anthropic, Google/DeepMind, GitHub developer-tool, AMD, ROCm, NVIDIA, vLLM, and Hugging Face announcement and release surfaces.
Reviewed AMD Advancing AI 2026 hardware and software announcements, including MI400, Helios, the Korea partnership, and ROCm.AI, before opening the linked primary artifacts.

Reviewed accessible X surfaces and search results for frontier researchers and AI infrastructure signals, including Andrej Karpathy, Jim Fan, Logan Kilpatrick, and AMD. No X content is used as article evidence.

alternatives.subject: AMD and Korea Ministry of Science and ICT sovereign AI partnership
alternatives.reason: The announcement is highly relevant to Korean readers, but the central commitments remain a partnership announcement without a versioned deployment plan, procurement scope, or executable technical artifact, so the central claim stays at E1.

alternatives.subject: GitHub Models full retirement on 2026-07-30
alternatives.reason: The shutdown deadline is operationally useful and officially confirmed, but it is a service policy change with no P2 artifact supporting an E2 central technical conclusion.

alternatives.subject: GitHub Copilot enterprise policy updates on 2026-07-27
alternatives.reason: The availability change is confirmed, but the newly published material does not establish a broader inspectable engineering change with an E2 center.

alternatives.subject: ROCm.AI public skills and ROCm CLI v0.1.0-experimental.1
alternatives.reason: A recent official announcement is backed by a fixed skills catalog, executable helper scripts, an exact CLI tag, downloadable Linux and Windows assets, checksums, signatures, and installer code. The same artifacts make the Tech Preview and planned-feature boundaries observable.

conflicts: AMD is the publisher and maintainer of ROCm.AI, AMD Skills, and ROCm CLI.
The public artifacts describe AMD's own supported workflows and do not constitute independent production validation.
No advance access, AMD hardware, vendor account, credits, sponsorship, advertising relationship, or embargo was provided.

claims.claim: AMD presents ROCm.AI as a unified experience across AMD Skills, ROCm CLI, ROCm Console, and Hyperloom, while public immutable artifacts currently provide an inspectable agent-skill catalog and ROCm CLI source and release.
claims.method: Compared AMD's 2026-07-23 product explanation with the immutable AMD Skills commit, ROCm CLI tag, source tree, and release assets.

sources.limitations: Vendor-authored product explanation; no independent benchmark or exact support matrix for the unified experience.
Tech Preview catalog maintained by the product owner; article did not execute the skills.
Experimental Tech Preview release; binaries were inspected as release metadata but not executed.

limitations: The article did not execute the end-to-end ROCm.AI workflow.
No public Hyperloom execution artifact or comparable benchmark was identified.
The public code does not prove the success rate of fresh-host setup or model serving.
conflict_of_interest: AMD describes and maintains its own developer experience and repositories.
recheck_triggers: Hyperloom public code, benchmark, or reproducible workload is released
ROCm.AI publishes a versioned support matrix or stable contract
Independent teams publish same-condition deployment results

claims.claim: ROCm CLI v0.1.0-experimental.1 publishes Linux and Windows x86_64 archives with SHA-256 and detached-signature sidecars, and its pinned Linux installer verifies the archive checksum before activation.
claims.method: Inspected the GitHub release API and page, tag ref, release assets, checksum sidecar, Cargo metadata, and install.sh at immutable commit cae77819a58ee8448a14160ce989832f500e6cc4.

sources.limitations: Release metadata marks prerelease false and uses stable wording even though the version is experimental and the README says Tech Preview.
Code inspection only; installer was not run and host mutations were not observed.
The article did not download and hash the 16,969,947-byte archive itself.
Project-authored trust design; organization-specific enforcement and trust roots require separate review.

limitations: The release binaries were not executed or independently reproduced from source.
Linux and Windows x86_64 assets do not prove support for every AMD GPU and operating system combination.
Signature assets existing does not prove a downstream deployment requires signature verification.
conflict_of_interest: The project owner publishes the binaries, checksums, signatures, installer, and trust documentation.
recheck_triggers: A non-experimental stable release is published
Independent reproducible-build or installer audit results are published
The release support matrix and rollback contract become versioned

claims.claim: At AMD Skills commit 228980933abd97a8aa4a2656c8ea3ae9e8b590c7, the catalog links usable local-AI, serving, kernel-evaluation, and trace-analysis skills while marking rocm-doctor, hyperloom-kernel-optimizer, apu-memory-tuner, and other entries as planned; some planned work is visible under staging.
claims.method: Inspected README catalog rows, repository tree, individual skill files, helper scripts, and staging paths at the immutable commit.

sources.limitations: Tech Preview catalog may change frequently.
Instruction and scripts are inspectable, but the article did not run them on Instinct hardware.
A staging directory is not a supported catalog entry or production contract.

limitations: Repository presence does not establish stable support or successful execution.
Federated skills depend on upstream pinned commits and external tools.
The exact catalog can change after the inspected commit.
conflict_of_interest: AMD owns the catalog and chooses which workflows and limitations to encode.
recheck_triggers: Planned entries move into the supported catalog
The catalog publishes versioned compatibility and deprecation policy
Behavioral evaluation results are published for the relevant skills

claims.claim: The fixed ROCm CLI README describes examine, SDK installation, model serving, dashboard telemetry, and chat, labels the software Tech Preview, and limits live dashboard telemetry to Linux or WSL.
claims.method: Inspected README and source layout at tag commit cae77819a58ee8448a14160ce989832f500e6cc4.

sources.limitations: Project documentation, not an independent compatibility test.
Source availability supports inspection and buildability, not hardware compatibility across all paths.

limitations: Synthetic demo mode is not evidence of real GPU telemetry or inference.
The article did not build the Rust workspace.
Command and behavior stability are explicitly not guaranteed.
conflict_of_interest: The CLI authors document their own feature and support boundaries.
recheck_triggers: Windows live-telemetry support is documented and tested
A stable CLI contract replaces the Tech Preview warning

claims.claim: Teams should approve AMD Skills instructions and ROCm CLI host mutations separately, pin immutable revisions, and expand agent permissions only after sandbox installation and a fixed-model smoke test pass.
claims.method: Derived from the mutable Tech Preview catalog, the skill's shell and Docker workflow, the CLI installer's filesystem behavior, and the release maturity limits.

sources.limitations: Does not define an organization-specific approval policy.
Workflow-specific instructions do not replace local security and change-management controls.
Filesystem and shell-profile changes depend on installer configuration and host state.

limitations: The recommended gates require adaptation to each organization's threat model and hardware fleet.
No measured productivity benefit is claimed.
conflict_of_interest: No vendor access or sponsorship; judgment is derived from public artifacts.
recheck_triggers: The project publishes an enterprise rollout and rollback guide
Independent production incident or success-rate data changes the risk model
